summary: Tacalcitol is a topical vitamin D3 analogue used once daily for chronic plaque psoriasis. It acts on the vitamin D receptor in keratinocytes to normalise the excessive proliferation and abnormal differentiation that characterise psoriatic plaques. It is not FDA-approved in the US (marketed in Europe/Japan as Curatoderm and others); this record is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF. It is generally well tolerated, with mild local irritation being the main effect; exceeding the recommended maximum amount risks hypercalcaemia/hypercalciuria.

moa: Tacalcitol is an analogue of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 that binds the vitamin D receptor in epidermal keratinocytes, inhibiting their excessive proliferation and promoting normal differentiation. It also has local immunomodulatory effects on inflammatory mediators, collectively reducing the scaling, thickness and erythema of psoriatic plaques.

Severe renal impairment with extensive application

preg: There are limited data in pregnancy; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk and avoid extensive application. Animal data with high systemic vitamin D doses suggest caution.
lact: It is not known whether tacalcitol is excreted in breast milk after topical use; use with caution and avoid applying to the breast to prevent infant ingestion.
renal: Use cautiously in renal impairment; reduced calcium clearance increases the theoretical risk of hypercalcaemia/hypercalciuria with extensive or prolonged use.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required for topical use; systemic exposure with correct use is low.

missed: If a once-daily application is missed, apply it when remembered, or simply continue with the next scheduled application the following day. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical overdose (excessive amount or area) can cause hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria. Stop the product, check serum and urinary calcium, ensure adequate hydration, and manage hypercalcaemia supportively; calcium levels normalise after discontinuation.
